observed: ui/watchlist_panel.py::remove_symbol re-indexes _row_data with `{(r-1 if r > row else r): values ...}` but never drops the removed row's own _row_data key. When the removed row is the LAST (max-index) row no later key overwrites it, so a stale `_row_data[row]` entry survives. Reviewer offscreen reproduction: a 3-row panel (AAPL/MSFT/TSLA), `remove_symbol('TSLA')` -> `table.rowCount() == 2` but `sorted(_row_data.keys()) == [0, 1, 2]` (stale key 2). Removing a middle row leaves `[0, 1]` because the shifted-up row overwrites the removed key — which is why tests/test_watchlist_add_remove_d22.py::test_D22_05_T02 (removes the middle row) does not catch it.
expected: remove_symbol's documented contract (docstring: 're-indexes ... `_row_data` keys') should leave no stale key: `_row_data` keys should always be exactly `range(rowCount())`, mirroring the explicit `_req_to_row` / `_prev_close` / `_last_price` / flash-timer handling.
suggested_direction: Drop the removed row's entry while re-indexing (e.g. `self._row_data.pop(row, None)` before/instead of relying on the shift) and add a last-row (and/or first-row) removal assertion to D22-05-T02 or a new D22-05 case so the branch is covered. Impact is currently benign — a key beyond `rowCount()` is never read, is overwritten by the next `add_symbol` at the same index, and `clear()` drops it — hence nice-to-have.
